subject: Renewal: rightsizing staircase onramp + ops checklist
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Rao <samira@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: rightsizing staircase onramp + ops checklist

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the quick sync today. Attached is a first-pass amendment and a sizing workbook to make the renewal mechanical. High-level proposal (short bullets to make reviews easier):

- Term: 36 months (co-term to Northbridge FY end 2028-06-30) with annual staircase onramp (Year 1 = 40% baseline, Year 2 = 70%, Year 3 = 100%)
- Autoscaling / burst: guaranteed burst pool for critical workloads (up to 2x baseline) with an explicit true-up quarterly
- Auto-renew: opt-in by default with a 60-day opt-out notice before renewal date; procurement can opt out earlier if needed
- Credits / onboarding: 12% onboarding credit applied in Q1 for migration and integration milestones (itemized in workbook)
- Billing: annual invoicing recommended; we can convert to quarterly true-ups if procurement requires cadence alignment

Attachments: Northbridge_Renewal_Amendment_v0.1.pdf (amendment stub), sizing_workbook.xlsx (workbook with token/traffic assumptions).

Can we set a 30-min call early next week to walk procurement through the workbook and confirm whether quarterly true-ups are required for you? Proposed times: Tue/9:00–11:00 PT or Wed/13:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

Date: 2025-09-03T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: rightsizing staircase onramp + ops checklist

Hi Evelyn —

Appreciate the summary and attachments. A few quick notes from procurement/ops after skimming:

- We need a quarterly true-up cadence (finance requires regular reconciliation).
- Can we co-term to our FY (2026-07-01 start aligned to 2028-06-30 end) — co-terming is a hard requirement for our reporting.
- Security is still doing a short re-review; will loop in our InfoSec lead if any new attestations are required.
- Pricing: can you provide a Year 1 example invoice (with onboarding credit applied) and call out any change in unit pricing if we convert from annual to quarterly invoices?

Looping in procurement: Northbridge Health Procurement <procurement@northbridgehealth.com>.

We can do Wed/14:00 PT to walk the workbook.

Best,
Samira Rao
Director, Product Ops — Northbridge Health
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-03T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: rightsizing staircase onramp + ops checklist (internal)

Karthik / Marissa —

Samira wants quarterly true-ups and co-term to their FY. Security re-review may add a week. Quick suggestion before the Wed call:

- Offer: convert billing to quarterly true-ups (same ARR annualized) but keep a 10% first-year onboarding discount and maintain the 12% onboarding credit tied to milestone sign-offs.
- Concession budget: I can go to 10% off Year 1 list and keep the onboarding credits. If we also add an SLO credit for latency > 250ms we could keep pricing intact.
- Ask: Marissa, do we have flexibility on the SLO credit bands (we typically use a 3% credit for single-month miss, escalating to 8% for repeated misses).

I want to avoid redoing the ramp math on the call; I'll bring a worked example showing Year 1 invoice with the credit apportionment. If we agree, I'll update the amendment and DocuSign link prior to the call.

Thanks,
Evelyn
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-03T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: rightsizing staircase onramp + ops checklist (internal)

Evelyn —

Agree with the approach. A couple of suggested guardrails:

- SLO credit: propose 3% credit for a single missed month, 6% for two months in a rolling 12, and 12% cap for the year. Call this out explicitly so procurement knows the downside is limited.
- Onboarding credit: tie 50% of the onboarding credit to “production traffic accepted” milestone (gives us leverage if integration lags).
- Implementation milestone: require a 90-day onboarding window from signature with a named Customer Success POC (we should include Marissa as CS lead).

If procurement accepts the quarterly invoicing with same annualized spend, we keep unit economics intact. I approve a one-time 10% Year 1 discount from our list rate. Get the updated amendment out with DocuSign and I’ll sign off.

— Karthik
VP, Revenue Operations

- Co-terms to Northbridge FY (end 2028-06-30)
- Offers quarterly true-ups (same annualized ARR) with the billing cadence reflected in Section 2.3
- Applies a 10% Year 1 list discount and preserves the 12% onboarding credit; 50% of onboarding credit tied to production acceptance milestone
- SLO credits are defined: 3% single-month, 6% for two months in a rolling 12, 12% annual cap
- Onboarding window: 90 days from signature; named CS lead (Marissa Cole) will run integration checklist and quarterly health reviews

Evelyn / team —

Thanks for the clean update and the walk-through earlier. Procurement reviewed v0.2 and we have two final asks before routing to legal for redlines:

1) Can the onboarding credit be split across Q1 and Q2 instead of front-loading Q1? This helps our cashflow recognition.
2) Procurement requests a standard 45-day net payment term rather than annual prepay.

If you can confirm those two, we’ll push to legal and aim to have an executed amendment in the next 10 business days. DocuSign timeline: procurement will try to turn on their side within 3 business days once legal returns redlines.
